title: Adaptive Beaconing: probabilistic spike isolation and alert routing for usage/cost/latency
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
The current console alerting for usage/cost/latency produces high noise (many low-signal alerts) and sometimes misses short-lived but high-impact spikes that drive billing or SLA breaches. Existing thresholding is static per-metric and doesn't account for exposure (customer volume), multi-modal seasonality across customers, or correlated signals across cost/latency/throughput.

Goal:
Design and deploy an â€˜Adaptive Beaconingâ€™ service: a lightweight probabilistic anomaly scoring and routing layer that ingests metric aggregates and emits prioritized alerts with contextual metadata (exposure, cohort, related-delta signatures). The service should:
- Reduce alert fatigue by suppressing low-probability noise while surfacing high-confidence incidents.
- Route alerts to the appropriate escalation channel and playbook (e.g., paging for high-latency customer-impact vs. slack for cost anomalies).
- Support coarse-grained canary rollout (internal -> beta customers -> all) and operate within existing SLOs for latency and cost.

High-level design (components):
1) Preprocessing pipeline (metrics-processor): compute normalized features per timeseries window (exposure-normalized rate, seasonality factor, short/long EWMA, delta-quantiles). Backfill scripts to compute features for a 90-day training/eval window.
2) Beacon scoring service (beacon-scorer): ensemble scorer using weighted heuristics + lightweight ML (robust z-score + EWMA slope + isolation score). Returns: score (0-1), confidence tag (low/medium/high), contributing features.
3) Routing & suppression layer (anomaly-router): policy engine driven by routing table (by metric, customer tier, release), auto-mutes, escalation mapping to PagerDuty/Slack/Email, and an adaptive cooldown.
4) Observability & eval harness: centralized dashboard (Grafana) showing precision/recall curves vs historical incidents, and a replay harness to measure false positive reduction.

Data pipeline changes required:
- New Kafka topic: telemetry.anom.features (schema: metric_key, window_start, window_end, exposure, features_json, raw_agg_refs)
- Metrics-processor runs in k8s as a cron/stream job and writes features to topic + BigQuery for offline eval.
- Beacon-scorer exposes HTTP endpoint /score and emits alerts to alerts.inbox topic for downstream router.
- Add feature toggle flags (FF) for beta routing and per-customer opt-in.

Evaluation and acceptance criteria:
- Backtest on 90 days of telemetry: reduce total alert volume by >=40% while retaining >=90% of incidents with severity >= high (severity labels derived from past runbooks).
- End-to-end scoring latency < 500ms p95 for an incoming feature batch of 50 timeseries.
- False positive rate for internal metrics <= 5% after tune-in.
- Successful canary: flagged customers (internal + 3 beta tenants) for 2 weeks with human-in-loop feedback.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Full ML model vs heuristic ensemble: chosen ensemble for lower ops cost, easier interpretability, and faster rollout. We may add a lightweight supervised model later if ensemble plateau.
- Centralized scoring vs per-region: start centralized (single scorer cluster) with region-aware features; split if latency becomes an issue.
- Sampling rate vs fidelity: expose FF to increase sampling for beta customers; default lower sampling to control ingestion cost.

Security and compliance notes:
- No customer PII in features. Exposure is an aggregate integer. All topics use existing Kafka ACLs and messages are encrypted in transit.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0-2: implement metrics-processor + backfill (internal metrics only).
- Week 2-4: deploy beacon-scorer in staging, run daily replay tests, iterate thresholds.
- Week 4-6: canary with internal + 3 beta customers, enable routing policies to slack only.
- Week 6-8: open to broader customers, enable PagerDuty for high-confidence incidents, automated runbook links.

Runbooks and follow-ups:
- Attach runbook template for each alert type (cost/latency/throughput) and map to playbooks in Confluence.
- Postmortem checklist to add incident labels for training/eval.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Adaptive+Beaconing+Design
- Eval dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/observability/ab-eval
- Backfill job PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/358
- Beacon-scorer service PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1246

Success metrics to track after GA:
- Monthly alert volume change (total & per-customer)
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for high-confidence alerts
- Cost delta in telemetry ingestion per month
- Customer escalations / support tickets related to missed incidents

Open questions / next steps:
- Determine initial default weights for ensemble and publish as FF defaults.
- Decide whether to persist per-customer baselines in Redis vs BigQuery cache for faster lookups.
- Chart of allowable cooldown windows per metric class to minimize saturation.
